text:
Alyssa Chen: seeing gRPC timeouts and RDMA handshakes failing for GPU pods in us-west2 since ~03:20 UTC. Pods restart after 1-2 mins.
Mike R: same here. Large packet pings between az-1 and az-2 show fragmentation + ~12-18% packet loss.
Samir Gupta: checking CNI drops - VXLAN fragments >1500 are being dropped on some nodes. Seems MTU mismatch across fleet (some 9000, some 1500).
Alyssa Chen: also saw 'rdma: connection reset by peer' in the workload logs and gRPC deadlines. Node conntrack is near full on a few hosts.
Tao Li: curious — did anyone push a default-deny netpol to that namespace? RDMA/control flows can rely on ephemeral ports and some non-TCP behavior.
Jen Patel: give me the netpol dump, I can look.
Alyssa Chen: pasted the suspect policy (trimmed):
```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-all-egress
  namespace: gpu-tenant-usw2
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress: []
```
Tao Li: yup that's the culprit. A baseline default-deny was merged without a companion allow for control-plane and intra-az pod CIDRs.
Mike R: combined with MTU mismatch, we're seeing fragmentation + drops + conntrack exhaustion because handshakes fail and retry a lot.
Samir Gupta: confirming on node az-2-03: ip -s link shows high RX errors on veth pairs, dmesg has 'fragments dropped', and calico logs show 'packet too large' for VXLAN.
Alyssa Chen: mitigation idea: apply a temporary allow-all egress policy scoped to GPU pods to restore traffic, then harden. I can apply now if folks agree.
Tao Li: agreed, do it. Then we should standardize MTU and patch conntrack limits.
Jen Patel: quick temp policy suggestion:
```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: temp-allow-egress-gpu
  namespace: gpu-tenant-usw2
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app_role: gpu-worker
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - {}
```
Alyssa Chen: applying via kubectl now (`kubectl apply -f -`)
ops-bot: deploy-bot: NetworkPolicy "temp-allow-egress-gpu" applied to namespace gpu-tenant-usw2 by alyssa
Alyssa Chen: within ~60s most RDMA handshakes recovered and gRPC errors dropped significantly. One pod still flaked - suspect stale conntrack entries. I'll cordon+drain if it doesn't recover.
Mike R: started a rolling restart of vxlan-enabled nodes in az-2 to rebalance MTU and clear bad state.
Samir Gupta: plan for next steps: (1) roll out uniform MTU 9000 for GPU fleet or document 1500 if we can't jumbo; (2) increase conntrack max and reduce timeout for RELATED/ESTABLISHED to handle bursts; (3) replace temp allow with explicit egress rules for kube-apiserver, cluster DNS, and intra-az pod CIDRs; (4) add CI gate for netpol changes.
Tao Li: +1. Also recommend a smoke test that runs a short RDMA/gRPC probe across AZs as part of netpolicy PR validation.
Leo Morales: I'll add two alerts: conntrack usage > 80% and netpolicy-deny spike > threshold. Also propose a periodic RDMA sidecar probe with 1s timeout, alert if >5% failure over 5m.
Jen Patel: I'll open a runbook PR with temp netpol revert, the proposed narrow rules, and rollback steps. Tagging Samir for MTU rollout and Tao for conntrack tuning.
Alyssa Chen: follow-up: cordoned the one flaky node, restarted pods, they came back healthy. Will monitor for 30m. Thanks for the quick triage.
Mike R: FYI I pushed a short script to infra repo that checks node MTU vs expected and lists mismatches. Put it in a PR.
Samir Gupta: also added Calico config note: enable jumbo frames handling and ensure iptables MTU passthrough for encapsulated traffic.
Alyssa Chen: once Jen has the PR I'll approve and we can schedule the MTU run during low-traffic window. Good catch everyone. :raised_hands:
